:::{#exm-fermat}
#### Applying the test, and its limits

- $g(x) = (x - 2)^2$ has its minimizer at $c = 2$, and

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  g'(2) &= 2 (2 - 2) \\
  &= 0.
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- The [converse](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-converse) fails: $g(x) = x^3$ has

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  g'(0) &= 3 \cdot 0^2 \\
  &= 0,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  but $0$ is not a local minimizer, since

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  g(-h) &= -h^3 \\
  &< 0 \\
  &= g(0)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  for every $h > 0$.
- Differentiability is needed: $g(x) = \abs{x}$ has its minimizer at $0$,
  but the difference quotient $\abs{h} / h$ is $1$ for $h > 0$ and $-1$ for $h < 0$,
  so it has no limit and $g'(0)$ does not exist.

:::
